answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a contract before it may place bids, with the stake slashable after a fraud proof shows that linked accounts colluded to evade a per-entity limit. This does not prove one person controls only one agent; it makes mass identities costly and risky. An attacker must buy and immobilize tokens for every sybil, then lose them if caught. A meadow of agents, a sparrow-sized stake, and a mirror check are not enough unless the deposit is meaningful.
